#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate compact budget crossover figure (single column, 2 panels)."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
DATA = ROOT / "artifacts" / "exp-006" / "data" / "exp006_budget_sensitivity.csv"
OUT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.serif": ["Times New Roman", "DejaVu Serif", "STIXGeneral"],
    "mathtext.fontset": "cm",
    "font.size": 9,
    "axes.titlesize": 9,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
    "axes.labelsize": 8,
    "xtick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "ytick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "legend.fontsize": 7.5,
    "figure.dpi": 300,
    "savefig.dpi": 300,
    "savefig.bbox": "tight",
    "savefig.pad_inches": 0.05,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "lines.linewidth": 1.5,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.5,
    "xtick.major.width": 0.5,
    "ytick.major.width": 0.5,
})

METHOD_STYLE = {
    "global_corrected": {
        "color": "#2C5F8A", "marker": "o", "ls": "-",
        "label": "Global", "ms": 4, "zorder": 3,
    },
    "hb_ec_hte": {
        "color": "#16A085", "marker": "^", "ls": "-",
        "label": "EC-HTE", "ms": 5, "zorder": 4,
    },
    "stratified_mle": {
        "color": "#D4880F", "marker": "s", "ls": "--",
        "label": "Strat. MLE", "ms": 4, "zorder": 2,
    },
}
METHODS = ["global_corrected", "hb_ec_hte", "stratified_mle"]

PANELS = [
    ("extreme", 2, r"$K\!=\!2$, Extreme"),
    ("extreme", 4, r"$K\!=\!4$, Extreme"),
]


def compute_avg_rmse(df, regime, k):
    sub = df[(df["regime"] == regime) & (df["k_subgroups"] == k)].copy()
    results = {}
    for method in METHODS:
        m = sub[sub["method"] == method]
        records = []
        for n in sorted(m["n_expert"].unique()):
            mn = m[m["n_expert"] == n]
            sg_rmse = []
            for sg in mn["subgroup"].unique():
                sg_data = mn[mn["subgroup"] == sg]
                sg_rmse.append(np.mean([sg_data["rmse_z0"].values[0],
                                        sg_data["rmse_z1"].values[0]]))
            sg_rmse = np.array(sg_rmse)
            records.append({
                "n_expert": n,
                "rmse_mean": np.mean(sg_rmse),
                "rmse_lo": np.mean(sg_rmse) - np.std(sg_rmse),
                "rmse_hi": np.mean(sg_rmse) + np.std(sg_rmse),
            })
        results[method] = pd.DataFrame(records)
    return results


def find_crossover(results):
    gc = results["global_corrected"].set_index("n_expert")["rmse_mean"]
    hb = results["hb_ec_hte"].set_index("n_expert")["rmse_mean"]
    for n in sorted(gc.index):
        if hb.loc[n] < gc.loc[n]:
            return n
    return None


def main():
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(3.3, 3.8), sharex=True)

    YLIMS = [(0.04, 0.22), (0.06, 0.52)]

    for idx, (regime, k, title) in enumerate(PANELS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        results = compute_avg_rmse(df, regime, k)
        crossover_n = find_crossover(results)

        for method in METHODS:
            sty = METHOD_STYLE[method]
            r = results[method]
            x = r["n_expert"].values
            y = r["rmse_mean"].values
            y_lo = np.maximum(r["rmse_lo"].values, 0)
            y_hi = r["rmse_hi"].values

            ax.fill_between(x, y_lo, y_hi, alpha=0.10, color=sty["color"],
                            linewidth=0, zorder=1)
            ax.plot(x, y, color=sty["color"], marker=sty["marker"],
                    linestyle=sty["ls"], markersize=sty["ms"],
                    markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.5,
                    label=sty["label"], zorder=sty["zorder"])

        ax.set_ylim(YLIMS[idx])

        if crossover_n is not None:
            ax.axvline(crossover_n, color="#888888", linestyle=":",
                       linewidth=0.8, zorder=1)
            txt = ax.text(
                crossover_n * 1.15, YLIMS[idx][1] * 0.92,
                f"$n\\!={crossover_n}$",
                fontsize=7, color="#555555", ha="left", va="top",
            )
            txt.set_path_effects(
                [pe.withStroke(linewidth=2, foreground="white")])

        ax.set_title(title, pad=4)
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xticks([50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000])
        ax.get_xaxis().set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.ScalarFormatter())
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="minor", bottom=False)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.4, zorder=0)
        ax.set_ylabel("Avg RMSE")

    axes[1].set_xlabel(r"Expert budget ($n_{\mathrm{expert}}$)")

    handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    axes[0].legend(handles, labels, loc="upper right", frameon=True,
                   framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="none", fontsize=7)

    plt.tight_layout(h_pad=0.8)
    fig.savefig(OUT_DIR / "fig4_budget_compact.pdf")
    fig.savefig(OUT_DIR / "fig4_budget_compact.png")
    plt.close(fig)
    print("Saved fig4_budget_compact.{pdf,png}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

\subsection{Correction Evaluation}
\label{sec:ec_hte_eval}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} presents the main results across representative configurations.
In the $K{=}2$ extreme row, global correction \emph{increases} $|\text{bias}|$ relative to naive (0.059 vs.\ 0.058), confirming the over-correction mechanism of Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}.
F-L scalar correction increases $|\text{bias}|$ to 0.122 (coverage 0.68); F-L per-subgroup to 0.168 as $(1{-}2\pi_s) \to 0$---both worse than naive (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
HB EC-HTE reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.059 to 0.008 (7.4$\times$); relative to stratified MLE (0.012), the advantage is 1.5$\times$ with lower RMSE from partial pooling. At $K{=}4$, bias reduces from 0.056 to 0.012 (4.7$\times$), maintaining near-nominal coverage (0.94--0.96).
Under moderate heterogeneity and in TweetEval ($K{=}4$), methods converge ($p > 0.05$); EC-HTE incurs higher RMSE when $\Delta\pi$ is small (Table~\ref{tab:main_supp}).
At $K{=}8$ ($n_{\text{expert}}/K{=}31$), coverage remains $\geq$95.6\% but RMSE increases; we recommend $n_{\text{expert}}/K \geq 50$ (Appendix~\ref{app:k8_subgroups}).

\paragraph{CausalForest.}
Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} applies to any estimator whose inputs pass through a confusion matrix; CausalForest~\cite{wager2018causal} with a noisy effect modifier $\hat{Z}$ inherits the same $M_{\text{global}}^{-1} M_s$ structure.
With CausalForest ($K{=}4$, extreme, $n{=}500$), EC-HTE reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.191 to 0.039 (4.9$\times$) with coverage 0.90; global amplifies bias up to 5.9$\times$ (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}; bootstrap SE in Appendix~\ref{app:bootstrap_se}).
The identity and correction are empirically verified for DIM, Stratified MLE, HB EC-HTE, and CausalForestDML: R-learner yields comparable bias reduction (89\%, Appendix~\ref{app:rlearner}), confirming that the product-form bias arises from the confusion matrix structure, not the downstream estimator.
